1.text_clean:
1. A sphere fits inside a cube.
[Diagram: sphere inscribed in a cube]
The length of the cube and the diameter of the sphere are $10.0 \pm 0.2$ cm.
What is the ratio $\dfrac{\text{percentage uncertainty of the volume of the sphere}}{\text{percentage uncertainty of the volume of the cube}}$?
A. $\frac{3}{4\pi}$
B. 1
C. 2
D. 8

2.text_clean:
2. An aircraft is moving horizontally. A parachutist leaves the aircraft and a few seconds later opens her parachute. Which graph shows the variation of the vertical speed $v$ with time $t$ for the parachutist from the time she leaves the aircraft until just before landing?
A. [Graph: v rises from 0 and levels off, then drops sharply and levels off at a lower constant value]
B. [Graph: v rises from 0 and levels off at a constant value]
C. [Graph: v starts high and decreases, levelling off at a low value]
D. [Graph: v starts high and decreases to zero, then dips negative sharply and returns towards zero]

3.text_clean:
3. An object of mass $m$ rests on a horizontal plane. The angle $\theta$ that the plane makes with the horizontal is slowly increased from zero. When $\theta = \theta_0$, the object begins to slide. What are the coefficient of static friction $\mu_s$ and the normal reaction force $N$ of the plane at $\theta = \theta_0$?
| | $\mu_s$ | $N$ |
A. | $\sin\theta_0$ | $mg\cos\theta_0$
B. | $\tan\theta_0$ | $mg\sin\theta_0$
C. | $\sin\theta_0$ | $mg\sin\theta_0$
D. | $\tan\theta_0$ | $mg\cos\theta_0$

4.text_clean:
4. A ball with mass $m$ moves horizontally with speed $u$. The ball hits a vertical wall and rebounds in the opposite direction with speed $v < u$. The duration of the collision is $T$. What are the magnitude of the average force exerted by the wall on the ball and the loss of kinetic energy of the ball?
| | Average force | Loss of kinetic energy |
A. | $\frac{m(u+v)}{T}$ | $\frac{m(u^2-v^2)}{2}$
B. | $\frac{m(u+v)}{T}$ | $\frac{m(u-v)^2}{2}$
C. | $\frac{m(u-v)}{T}$ | $\frac{m(u^2-v^2)}{2}$
D. | $\frac{m(u-v)}{T}$ | $\frac{m(u-v)^2}{2}$

5.text_clean:
5. A train on a straight horizontal track moves from rest at constant acceleration. The horizontal forces on the train are the engine force and a resistive force which increases with speed. Which graph represents the variation with time $t$ of the power $P$ developed by the engine?
A. [Graph: P constant (horizontal line)]
B. [Graph: P increases linearly from the origin]
C. [Graph: P rises steeply from the origin then levels off]
D. [Graph: P increases from the origin with increasing gradient (curving upwards)]

6.text_clean:
6. The graph shows how the acceleration $a$ of an object varies with distance travelled $x$.
[Graph: $a$ / m s$^{-2}$ against $x$ / m; $a$ = 20 constant from $x$ = 0 to 15 m, then decreases linearly to 0 at $x$ = 25 m]
The mass of the object is 3.0 kg. What is the total work done on the object?
A. 300 J
B. 400 J
C. 1200 J
D. 1500 J

7.text_clean:
7. A container with 0.60 kg of a liquid substance is placed on a heater at time $t = 0$. The specific latent heat of vaporization of the substance is 200 kJ kg$^{-1}$. The graph shows the variation of the temperature $T$ of the substance with time $t$.
[Graph: T against t / s; T rises linearly from t = 0 to 10 s, stays constant from 10 s to 50 s, then rises again to 60 s]
What is the power of the heater?
A. 1200 W
B. 3000 W
C. 4800 W
D. 13 300 W

8.text_clean:
8. Under what conditions of density and pressure is a real gas best described by the equation of state for an ideal gas?
A. Low density and low pressure
B. Low density and high pressure
C. High density and low pressure
D. High density and high pressure

9.text_clean:
9. Horizontally polarized light of intensity $I_0$ enters a polarizer P whose polarization axis makes an angle of $\theta$ degrees with the horizontal. Light from P is then incident on a polarizer A with fixed vertical polarization axis.
[Diagram: horizontally polarized light of intensity $I_0$ passes through polarizer P (axis at angle $\theta$ to horizontal) then polarizer A (vertical axis); transmitted light intensity $I$]
The angle $\theta$ is varied from 0 to 90 degrees. Which of the following represents the variation with $\theta$ of the intensity $I$ of the light transmitted through A?
A. [Graph: $I/I_0$ constant at 0.25 from 0 to 90°]
B. [Graph: $I/I_0$ rises from 0 at 0° to a maximum 0.25 at 45° and falls to 0 at 90°]
C. [Graph: $I/I_0$ zero for all $\theta$]
D. [Graph: $I/I_0$ falls from 0.5 at 0° to 0 at about 90°]

10.text_clean:
10. A pipe of length $L$ has two open ends. Another pipe of length $L'$ has one open end and one closed end.
The frequency of the first harmonic of both pipes is the same. What is $\frac{L'}{L}$?
A. 2
B. $\frac{3}{2}$
C. 1
D. $\frac{1}{2}$

11.text_clean:
11. A light ray passes from air to water as shown.
[Diagram: light ray incident obliquely from air onto an air–water boundary]
What are the change in the wavelength of the light wave and the change in the angle the ray makes with the normal to the surface?
| | Wavelength | Angle with normal |
A. | increases | increases
B. | increases | decreases
C. | decreases | increases
D. | decreases | decreases

12.text_clean:
12. A circuit consists of a cell of electromotive force (emf) 6.0 V and negligible internal resistance connected to two resistors of 4.0 Ω.
[Circuit: 6.0 V cell in series with ammeter A and two 4.0 Ω resistors in parallel; voltmeter V across the parallel resistors]
The ammeter has resistance equal to 1.0 Ω and the voltmeter is ideal. What are the readings of the ammeter and the voltmeter?
| | Ammeter | Voltmeter |
A. | 2.0 A | 3.0 V
B. | 3.0 A | 3.0 V
C. | 2.0 A | 4.0 V
D. | 3.0 A | 4.0 V

13. A wire carrying a current $I$ is placed in a region of uniform magnetic field $B$, as shown in the diagram.
[Diagram: straight wire of length $L$ at 45° (current $I$ towards top right) in a uniform field $B$ directed out of the page]
The direction of the field $B$ is out of the page and the length of the wire is $L$. What is correct about the direction and magnitude of the force acting on the wire?
| | Direction | Magnitude |
A. | ↘ (down-right) | equal to $BIL$
B. | ↘ (down-right) | smaller than $BIL$
C. | ↗ (up-right) | equal to $BIL$

14.text_clean:
14. A mass connected to one end of a rigid rod rotates at constant speed in a vertical plane about the other end of the rod.
[Diagram: mass on a rod moving in a vertical circle about the rod's fixed end; mass shown at the top]
The force exerted by the rod on the mass is
A. zero everywhere.
B. constant in magnitude.
C. always directed towards the centre.
D. a minimum at the top of the circular path.

15.text_clean:
15. A simple model of an atom has five energy levels. What is the maximum number of different frequencies in the emission spectrum of that atom?
A. 4
B. 6
C. 10
D. 25

16.text_clean:
16. Which of the following lists three fundamental forces in increasing order of strength?
A. electromagnetic, gravity, strong nuclear
B. weak nuclear, gravity, strong nuclear
C. gravity, weak nuclear, electromagnetic
D. electromagnetic, strong nuclear, gravity

17.text_clean:
17. Patterns in graphs help scientists make predictions. What can be deduced from a graph of neutron number versus proton number for all stable nuclides?
A. The short-range nature of the strong nuclear force
B. The increase of the binding energy per nucleon with proton number
C. The existence of quarks and leptons
D. The existence of alpha decay
17.note: Nuclear stability (N vs Z) / strong force range; tagged E.3 (nuclear stability, binding); X.2 also arguable.

18.text_clean:
18. A solar panel has surface area 0.40 m$^2$ and efficiency 50 %. The average intensity of radiation reaching the surface of the panel is 0.25 kW m$^{-2}$. What is the average power output from an array of 10 of these solar panels?
A. 0.5 W
B. 5 W
C. 50 W
D. 500 W

19.text_clean:
19. What is the correct order of energy transformations in a coal power station?
A. thermal → chemical → kinetic → electrical
B. chemical → thermal → kinetic → electrical
C. chemical → kinetic → thermal → electrical
D. kinetic → chemical → electrical → thermal

20.text_clean:
20. A black body of surface 1.0 m$^2$ emits electromagnetic radiation of peak wavelength $2.90 \times 10^{-6}$ m. Which of the following statements about the body are correct?
I. The temperature of the body is 1000 K.
II. The energy radiated by the body in one second is $5.7 \times 10^4$ J.
III. The body is a perfect absorber of electromagnetic radiation.
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

21.text_clean:
21. A mass is connected to a spring on a frictionless horizontal surface as shown.
[Diagram: mass attached to a horizontal spring fixed to a wall, on a frictionless surface]
The spring is extended beyond its equilibrium length and the mass executes simple harmonic motion (SHM). Which of the following is independent of the initial displacement of the spring?
A. The angular frequency of the oscillation
B. The total energy of the mass
C. The average speed of the mass
D. The maximum kinetic energy of the mass

22.text_clean:
22. A single-slit diffraction experiment is performed using light of different colours. The width of the central peak in the diffraction pattern is measured for each colour. What is the order of the colours that corresponds to increasing widths of the central peak?
A. red, green, blue
B. red, blue, green
C. blue, green, red
D. green, blue, red

23.text_clean:
23. In a double-slit interference experiment, the following intensity pattern is observed for light of wavelength $\lambda$.
[Graph: intensity of light / arbitrary units against diffraction angle / rad from −0.06 to 0.06; interference fringes spaced about 0.01 rad, with peak heights decreasing from 1.0 at the centre under a diffraction envelope]
The distance between the slits is $d$. What can be deduced about the value of the ratio $\frac{\lambda}{d}$ and the effect of single-slit diffraction in this experiment?
| | $\frac{\lambda}{d}$ | Single-slit diffraction |
A. | 100 | non-negligible
B. | 0.01 | non-negligible
C. | 100 | negligible
D. | 0.01 | negligible

24.text_clean:
24. A simple pendulum has mass $M$ and length $l$. The period of oscillation of the pendulum is $T$. What is the period of oscillation of a pendulum with mass $4M$ and length $0.25l$?
A. $0.5T$
B. $T$
C. $2T$
D. $4T$

25.text_clean:
25. A train moves at constant speed whilst emitting a sound wave of frequency $f_0$. At $t = t_0$ the train passes through a station. Which graph shows the variation with time $t$ of the frequency $f$ of the sound wave as measured by an observer standing on the station platform?
A. [Graph: f above $f_0$ and slowly rising, drops sharply at $t_0$ below $f_0$, then slowly rises]
B. [Graph: f constant at $f_0$]
C. [Graph: f rises to a peak at $t_0$ then falls]
D. [Graph: f constant above $f_0$, drops at $t_0$ to a constant value below $f_0$]

26. A negative charge moves in an electric field. Equipotential lines for the field and four possible paths of the charge are shown. Which path corresponds to the largest work done on the charge by the field?
[Diagram: three curved equipotentials V = 10 V (outer), 20 V, 30 V (inner); path A from 30 V to 10 V, path B from 10 V to 30 V, path C from 10 V to 20 V, path D from 20 V to 10 V]
A. A
B. B
C. C
D. D

27.text_clean:
27. In an experiment, oil droplets of mass $m$ and charge $q$ are dropped into the region between two horizontal parallel plates. The electric field $E$ between the plates can be adjusted. Air resistance is negligible. Which is correct when the droplets fall vertically at constant velocity?
A. $E = 0$
B. $E < \frac{mg}{q}$
C. $E = \frac{mg}{q}$
D. $E > \frac{mg}{q}$

28.text_clean:
28. A satellite orbits a planet. Which graph shows how the kinetic energy $E_K$, the potential energy $E_P$ and the total energy $E$ of the satellite vary with distance $x$ from the centre of the planet?
A. [Graph: $E_P$ positive decreasing curve; $E_K$ and $E$ negative curves]
B. [Graph: $E_K$ positive curve; $E$ negative curve above $E_P$ negative curve]
C. [Graph: $E$ positive curve; $E_K$ and $E_P$ negative curves]
D. [Graph: $E_K$ positive curve; $E_P$ negative curve above $E$ negative curve]

29. A coil of area $A$ is placed in a region of uniform horizontal magnetic field $B$. At $t = 0$, the coil starts to rotate with constant angular speed $\omega$ about a horizontal axis.
[Diagram: horizontal flat coil with terminals X and Y between two magnet poles; field B horizontal; rotation axis horizontal and parallel to B]
What is the emf between X and Y?
A. zero
B. $\omega AB\sin\omega t$
C. $AB\cos\omega t$
D. $-\omega AB\sin\omega t$

30.text_clean:
30. The diagram shows a conducting rod of length $L$ being moved in a region of uniform magnetic field $B$. The field is directed at right angles to the plane of the paper. The rod slides on conducting rails at a constant speed $v$. A resistor of resistance $R$ connects the rails.
[Diagram: rod of length L sliding with speed v along two parallel rails joined by resistor R, in field B]
What is the power required to move the rod?
A. zero
B. $\frac{vBL}{R}$
C. $\frac{v^2B^2L^2}{R}$
D. $\frac{v^2B^2L^2}{R^2}$

A. $\frac{\bar{P}}{2V_0}$
B. $\frac{\bar{P}}{\sqrt{2}V_0}$
C. $\frac{\sqrt{2}\bar{P}}{V_0}$
D. $\frac{2\bar{P}}{V_0}$

A. [Graph: V rises to a peak then shows small ripple with recharge peaks about every 3 ms, t / ms 0–12]
B. [Graph: full-wave rectified humps, peaks about every 3 ms]
C. [Graph: half-wave rectified humps about every 6.3 ms with zero in between]
D. [Graph: V rises to a peak, then decays with a recharge peak about every 6.3 ms]

A. | increases | increases
B. | increases | decreases
